result.markdown: --- title: >- [fmt_number()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Format a number with a fixed number of decimal places and a thousands separator. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/example-python-package/blob/main/tinytab/_formats.py#L46-L89){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fmt_number( x, *, decimals=2, sep_mark=",", ) ``` ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The number to format. [decimals]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The number of decimal places. [sep_mark]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[","]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The character used to separate groups of thousands. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The formatted number. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} By default, numbers get two decimal places and a comma between groups of thousands: ::: {#2e1a50c8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from tinytab import fmt_number fmt_number(1234567.891) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` '1,234,567.89' ``` ::: ::: Use `decimals=` to change the precision, and `sep_mark=` for a different separator: ::: {#26aa32c5 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} fmt_number(1234567.891, decimals=0, sep_mark=" ") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` '1 234 568' ``` ::: :::
